glass_data <- read_csv("https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/glass.data",
                       col_names = c("Id", "RI", "Na", "Mg", "Al", "Si", "K",
                                     "Ca", "Ba", "Fe", "Type"))


3 & 4.
Now we are going to overwrite the column Type as Type_of_glass, and replace the numbers to the corresponding type as factor.

glass_data |>
  mutate(Type_of_glass = factor(Type,
                                labels = c("building_windows_float_processed",
                                         "building_windows_non_float_processed",
                                         "vehicle_windows_float_processed",
                                         "containers",
                                         "tableware",
                                         "headlamps")),
         Type = NULL) |>
  filter(Fe < 0.2,
         Type_of_glass %in% c("tableware", "headlamps")) |>
  show()

Yeast data
We get the code from HW3

yeast_data <- read_table("https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/yeast.data",
                       col_names = c("seq_name", "mcg", "gvh", "alm", "mit", 
                                     "erl", "pox", "vac", "nuc", "class"))


── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cols(
  seq_name = col_character(),
  mcg = col_double(),
  gvh = col_double(),
  alm = col_double(),
  mit = col_double(),
  erl = col_double(),
  pox = col_double(),
  vac = col_double(),
  nuc = col_double(),
  class = col_character()
)



5 & 6.
We are going to remove two columns using the mutate function, and add the columns to the mean and median for each numeric variable.

yeast_data |>
  group_by(class) |>
  mutate(seq_name = NULL,
         nuc = NULL,
         across(where(is.numeric), 
                list(mean = mean, median = median),
                .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")) |>
  show()

Wine data
From HW3

library(readxl)

white_data <- read_excel("../HW3/white-wine.xlsx")

var_wine <- read_excel("../HW3/white-wine.xlsx",
                       sheet = excel_sheets("../HW3/white-wine.xlsx")[2])
#And we re-assign the colnames to the tibble with the data

colnames(white_data) <- var_wine$Variables #it is necessary to get the variable column as a vector of characters

white_data$type <- "white"

red_data <- read_delim("https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/red-wine.csv",
                       delim = ";",
                       col_names = var_wine$Variables,
                       skip = 1
                      )
red_data$type <- "red"

wine_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(white_data, red_data)


7, 8, 9, & 10.
We start by taking the wine data already created, and

wine_data |>
  filter(quality > 6.5,
         alcohol < 13.2) |> # We get the vales that have a high quality and reasonable alcohol content
  arrange(desc(quality)) |> #then we sorted in descending order on the quality variable
  select(contains("acid"), alcohol, quality, type) |> #just select the columns with acid, alcohol, quality, and type
  group_by(quality) |> #we group by quality to get means per quality group.
  mutate(alcohol_mean = mean(alcohol)) |>
  show()
